correctness.rationale: The exact pseudogradient is the gradient of a strictly convex quadratic potential; the transformed two-demand Beckmann optimizers are feasible because all parallel affine Wardrop link flows are nondecreasing in demand. This proves the universal identity and uniqueness including endpoints. The explicit two-road quadratic objective establishes the sharp threshold and cost gap. Independent exact-rational tests: 2100 general KKT instances and 1344 two-road identity instances.

originality.rationale: No exact shifted-demand symmetrization was identified in the three relevant inspected primary full texts or published mathematical-result similarity searches. The 2024 study gives monotonicity, the 2023 study gives restricted critical-fleet results, and the 2018 paper gives existence and solvers; those prior statements do not state or directly dominate the exact representation. The underlying game, strict convexity and Wardrop water filling are credited as prior art. Residual historical-priority uncertainty is explicitly disclosed.
residual_risks: Historical equivalent closed forms might exist in older multi-class transportation-equilibrium theory (including Harker 1988 and Yang et al. 2007), which was not exhaustively inspected in primary full text.
The underlying pseudogradient and strict convexity are established; the proposed novelty is confined to exact shifted-demand decoupling and sharp all-share allocation formulas.

value.rationale: An arbitrary-link coupled mixed Wardrop/atomic-fleet game is reduced exactly to two scalar monotone Wardrop inversions. This resolves all fleet shares and support transitions, and yields a sharp intervention-size plateau and efficiency law in an interpretable two-road example. The target is motivated by published open questions about precise coordination thresholds, and is a structural formula rather than a routine numerical recalculation.
